summary: Kazutoshi Soma is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a lecturer post at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Kazutoshi Ueda (1867–1937) was a linguist and Japanologist who studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Florenz, whom he succeeded. He also founded the Linguistic Society of Japan.

Kazuyoshi Hotta is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007) and Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo from 1942 to 1948. He served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989), vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993), and founded Shinnyokai.
Keenan W. Cox works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2014) under the supervision of James A. Benn.

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) studied Indology and religious studies at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University (~1960–1964) and was Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA, serving from circa 1967 to 1994.

Kehan Ding specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. After earning a PhD at the University of Edinburgh (2018–2024), Ding served Edinburgh as a Course Assistant (2019–2022) and Teaching Fellow (2025).

Kei Kataoka (born 1969) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University, where he is attested as professor in 2026.
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University, where he holds a faculty post (attested 2026).

Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Minoru Hara at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1997). He held research and teaching posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (1975) and Kokugakuin University (1986–1995).

Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from 1944 to 1947. He held academic posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1974) and Otani University (~1986–1995).
Keiji Kokubu (1907–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University and under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Nanzan University, Ritsumeikan University, and Ryukoku University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University and University of Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Hajime Tanabe, and Martin Heidegger. He taught at Otani University (~1927–1935) and Kyoto University, serving as professor from 1943 to 1964.

Keiki Nakayama works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020). He held posts at Kyoto University, the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2020), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Shukyo University (~1913–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1939), and was associate professor at Tokyo (~1924–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held research positions at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).

Keinin Hayashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1998, 2026) and formerly lectured at Waseda University.

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who completed a PhD at Durham University (2006–2010) under Robin Coningham. He lectured at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) before becoming Senior Lecturer in Asian Archaeology at La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1959). He held faculty posts at Koyasan University (1959–1973; visiting professor 2005–2009) and Kochi University (1973–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Tohoku University. He was a professor at Rissho University (~1970–1979), Emeritus Professor at Tohoku University (~1979–1993), and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–1999).
